skill.name: skill-store-publisher
skill.description: Push an existing SKILL.md skill (or a whole skill repo) to agent-skill marketplaces at home and abroad, free and paid. Use it when the user asks to publish / upload / list / 上架 / 推送 a skill to skill stores, skill marketplaces, 技能商店, 技能市场, plugin marketplaces, or asks why a published skill is not being discovered. Covers repo layout for auto-indexers, public submit APIs, GitHub-PR registries, login-gated CLIs, platform-hosted stores that need porting, and how to price a paid listing. 关键词：上架技能、推送技能、技能商店、技能市场、skill store、marketplace、publish skill、被收录、署名。
skill.summary: Prepare skill repositories, build distribution archives, and coordinate marketplace submissions with clear manual handoffs.

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts concern Markdown, scanner signatures, or expected publishing operations rather than executable threats. Confirmed risks include GitHub credential exposure through a third-party mirror, predictable authentication logs, and unsafe archive collection. Additional concerns involve misleading security assurances, identity-verification avoidance guidance, and a checksum that does not authenticate the distributed archive.

remediation.issue: GitHub authentication headers are sent to a third-party mirror in both Git troubleshooting recipes.
remediation.suggestion: Remove mirror authentication recipes and send GitHub credentials only to trusted GitHub endpoints. Rotate tokens used with this mirror.

remediation.issue: Authentication commands use a predictable shared temporary log without secure creation or explicit permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with restrictive permissions, avoid following symlinks, and delete authentication logs after login completes.

remediation.issue: Archive collection includes unfiltered secret files and follows file symlinks when reading archive contents.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinks and files outside the resolved skill root. Exclude credentials and secret files, and require users to inspect an archive manifest.

remediation.issue: Review guidance recommends security assurances without requiring verification against the submitted skill.
remediation.suggestion: Require evidence for every security claim, disclose actual network and write behavior, and prioritize fixing unsafe behavior over improving approval notes.

remediation.issue: Publishing guidance recommends a direct dashboard route to avoid an identity-verification introduction.
remediation.suggestion: Remove avoidance guidance and follow the documented verification process. Require the account owner to complete all mandatory identity checks.

remediation.issue: The generated archive checksum hashes concatenated source contents instead of the final ZIP file.
remediation.suggestion: Hash the completed ZIP bytes after closing the archive. Verify the checksum with a standard SHA-256 utility before distributing artifacts.

semantic_findings.title: Security Assurances Recommended Without Verification
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md recommends no-network, no-eval, and backup assurances in submission notes as more effective than code changes. These claims lack required verification and can mislead reviewers about actual behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions prioritize assurances and added explanations without conditioning each claim on implementation evidence. This creates review-integrity risk, although intentional deception is not established.

semantic_findings.title: Identity Verification Avoidance Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The recipe recommends opening /dashboard/publish directly to avoid a /dashboard/verify identity and face-verification introduction. This encourages circumventing onboarding safeguards rather than confirming platform requirements.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The avoidance route and verification page are explicitly stated. Server-side bypass is not demonstrated, and the following sentence reserves identity verification for the user.

semantic_findings.title: Archive Checksum Does Not Authenticate the Archive
semantic_findings.description: The .sha256 sidecar and manifest label a concatenated source-content hash as the ZIP checksum. Archive bytes, filenames, and boundaries are not authenticated by this value.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The hash receives only each file's data before ZIP serialization. The sidecar names the ZIP despite never hashing its final bytes.

content.user_title: Prepare and Submit Skills to Marketplaces
content.value_statement: Skill marketplaces require different repository layouts, packages, and submission steps. This skill provides preflight checks, archive building, API submissions, and manual publishing guidance.
actual_capabilities: Check skill metadata, repository layout, licensing, file sizes, referenced documents, and textual security patterns.
Build a ZIP with SKILL.md at its root, exclude common development files, and generate a package manifest.
Submit repository URLs to configured Skillstore and SkillsMD endpoints.
Upload a selected skill document and contact details through Skillbay multipart submission.
Query Skillstore submission status and display channel requirements, supported methods, and manual follow-up steps.
Provide recipes for repository metadata, GitHub PR submissions, authenticated CLI publishing, and paid listing preparation.
limitations: Marketplace approval, indexing, and API availability are external dependencies; documented requirements and pricing need independent verification.
Login, identity verification, seller onboarding, and platform-specific porting require separate user actions.
Security checks are heuristic; archive handling, mirror authentication recipes, temporary logs, and generated checksums need remediation.
The skills.sh probe and some fallback metadata are hardcoded to the author's example project.

use_cases.title: Prepare a First Skill Release
use_cases.description: Review metadata, licensing, package contents, and repository layout before selecting a submission channel.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multiple Distribution Channels
use_cases.description: Track API submissions, PR receipts, login requirements, and platform-specific work in one release checklist.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Paid Listing
use_cases.description: Organize listing fields, comparison examples, account prerequisites, and pricing questions without assuming anonymous submission creates a paid product.

prompt_templates.title: Review Publishing Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [skill directory] for metadata, licensing, repository layout, and package readiness. Report issues without modifying files or contacting marketplaces.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Distribution Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a packaging plan for [repository] and [skill directory]. Identify secrets, symlinks, and excluded files before building any archive.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Selected API Submissions
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare submissions for [repository] to [selected channels]. Show destinations and exact data first. Submit only after approval, then retain receipts and manual handoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Multi-Channel Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the release plan for [skill]. Verify security claims, channel requirements, archive contents, and checksums. Reject mirror credential forwarding and verification avoidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: review security and release integrity.

output_examples.input: Review a skill before its first marketplace submission.
output: Readiness review: metadata is present, but licensing and package contents still need confirmation.
Next action: inspect the distribution file list and remove secrets before packaging.
Publication status: no marketplace was contacted.
API channels: confirm destinations and submitted data before sending requests.
Authenticated channels: wait for the account owner to complete login and required verification.
Hosted platforms: estimate porting separately from repository publication.
Completion record: retain submission identifiers and PR links; pending review does not mean approval.

output_examples.input: Prepare requirements for a paid marketplace listing.
output: Listing materials: title, summary, detailed description, package, and comparison examples.
Account requirements: confirm seller eligibility and payment onboarding with the selected marketplace.
Pricing status: verify current terms; anonymous quick submission does not configure a paid listing.

best_practices: Inspect packages for secrets and symlinks, then independently calculate checksums from final archive bytes.
Verify marketplace requirements and every security claim before publishing; send credentials only to their intended trusted service.
Approve external destinations and payloads explicitly, retain receipts, and separate submitted, pending-login, and porting states.
anti_patterns: Sending GitHub authorization headers through third-party mirrors or leaving authentication logs in predictable shared files.
Submitting every channel without reviewing disclosed data, package contents, or required identity checks.
Claiming guaranteed approval, no-network behavior, verified checksums, or paid listing creation without supporting evidence.

faq.question: Can this publish to every marketplace automatically?
faq.answer: No. It automates selected HTTP submissions and provides guidance for PR, CLI, and manual channels. Hosted platforms may require separate development.

faq.question: Do the included Python scripts need third-party packages?
faq.answer: The Python scripts use the standard library. Optional workflows depend on tools such as GitHub CLI, npm, and marketplace-specific CLIs.

faq.question: Which information can leave my machine?
faq.answer: Depending on the channel, submissions send repository URLs, notes, contact details, or the selected skill document. Review each destination and payload first.

faq.question: Does a successful submission mean the listing is live?
faq.answer: No. A receipt confirms submission, not approval or indexing. Security review, moderation, login, or seller onboarding may remain outstanding.

faq.question: Can anonymous submission set a paid price?
faq.answer: The included quick-submission workflows do not configure paid seller listings. Confirm current seller onboarding, payment requirements, and pricing controls directly with the marketplace.

faq.question: Does passing preflight prove that a package is secure?
faq.answer: No. Preflight uses heuristic text checks. Review archive contents, credential handling, authentication logs, and security claims independently before publishing.
